unavailable_fields.pcie_bytes: Hardware counters require a successful collector-specific probe; the observed NVML pcie.tx/rx (390/341 KB/s) and gpu_utilization (0%) are idle-window device-wide samples and cannot yield per-step or per-collective bytes; not derivable from the 497759232 logical payload bytes.
unavailable_fields.nvlink_bytes: Hardware counters require a successful collector-specific probe; additionally the observed transport is SHM/direct/direct with peer_access 0->1 and 1->0 disabled, so no NVLink P2P path is in use to attribute bytes to; retained unknown.
unavailable_fields.hardware_utilization: Hardware counters require a successful collector-specific probe; available NVML utilization is device-wide with native sampling windows (observed 0% at idle), not per-collective utilization.
unavailable_fields.per_collective_wire_bytes: device_telemetry provides device-wide rates with native windows, not per-collective bytes; PCIe/NVLink traffic must not be invented from logical payload or memcpy sizes; stays unknown.
unavailable_fields.nccl_wait_vs_wire_separation: Nsys timelines alone do not separate NCCL in-kernel waiting from wire transfer, and kernel durations include waiting (matched collectives: rank 1 ~14-20 ms vs rank 0 ~3.3 ms for 28.35 MB; final 157.5 MB symmetric at ~19.7 ms); only bounds and reference experiments can be reported.
unavailable_fields.gpu_readiness_and_consumer_completion: execution_timeline reports clock alignment bounds for matching CPU submissions only; GPU readiness and consumer completion may remain unknown, and cross-rank timestamps use no clock subtraction policy.

plan.rationale: Objective is max-rank summed NCCL kernel duration of the accumulated step (rank 1 = 213.058 ms vs rank 0 = 59.526 ms, so rank 1 dominates), under a step_ms <= 1.05x baseline constraint. The torch collector already ran and supplies the objective field plus full collective/kernel, bucket-inventory and payload evidence; it is not re-selected. (1) nccl_tuning: all 13 kernels are named ncclDevKernel_AllReduce_Sum_f32_RING_LL, but kernel entry names alone do not identify the protocol; actual algorithm/protocol/channel decisions in a warmed worker are needed to know whether the LL choice at 28.35 MB and 157.54 MB fp32 over SHM/direct/direct (peer access disabled both directions) is a tunable lever, especially for the symmetric ~19.7 ms final 157.54 MB allreduce. (2) collective_calibration: a synthetic full-world SUM allreduce at the actually observed sizes/dtypes (7,087,872 and 39,385,344 fp32) with correctness checks gives clean reference durations that separate inherent collective cost from in-step in-kernel waiting on rank 1; treated as a reference experiment, not a performance lower bound or critical-path estimate. (3) execution_timeline: rank 1 starts each small collective ~10.3-10.9 ms before rank 0 and waits in-kernel (4.2-6.1x duration skew on 12 of 13 collectives), so CPU-to-CUDA submit associations, synchronization and per-device intervals with reported clock alignment bounds are the right instruments for submit-side attribution of the skew; it never replaces a communication hook. (4) nsys: available and useful for the open overlap/attribution questions - compute overlap is only 4.073/10.373 ms of 59.526/213.058 ms union and coverage reports 208 ambiguous forward sequences; caveat that nsys alone does not separate NCCL waiting from wire transfer and bucket identity is already observed via gradient-storage membership, so no extra bucket-proof burden is placed on it. Excluded: device_telemetry (device-wide NVML windows, not per-collective bytes; idle samples already observed; cannot advance a kernel-duration objective), python_runtime (no host-dispatch evidence; perturbs execution and yields non-clean inclusive/self times), binding_cost and candidate_diagnostics (no candidate exists yet), torch ( already ran).
